subject: Economics

objectives.name: Show that you understand the economics you have studied and current economic evidence; include extension content if you take HL.

Apply economic ideas to actual situations, interpret the evidence and explain how it is being used. In your IA, connect each commentary to its key concept; at HL, also apply and analyse extension content.
Build and evaluate an economic argument using theory and examples. At HL, also evaluate extension content and use economic evidence to recommend policy.
Organize your writing with accurate economic terminology. Use diagrams, news extracts, data and calculations to explain and analyse economic relationships.

components.name: Portfolio of three commentaries (SL)

criteria.name: Diagrams
criteria.guidance: Accurate, labelled, and actually referred to in the text. A diagram nobody discusses earns little.

criteria.name: Terminology
criteria.guidance: Use the economic terms the article calls for, consistently, not once in the introduction.

criteria.name: Application and analysis
criteria.guidance: Explain the economics of this specific situation. Summarising the article is not application.

criteria.name: Key concept
criteria.guidance: One concept per commentary, integrated throughout — naming it and moving on forfeits the marks.

criteria.name: Evaluation
criteria.guidance: Stakeholders, short run versus long run, and assumptions. One-sided evaluation caps the mark.

notes: Three commentaries, each on a different published article, a different syllabus unit and a different key concept.
Each commentary is 800 words maximum and marked out of 14 across five criteria; 3 further portfolio-level marks give a total of 45.
Criterion NAMES are corroborated; the per-criterion mark split is NOT — sources disagree, so no marks are published.
Articles must be from different sources and published within a year of the commentary.
At SL this is 30% of the subject — the highest-weighted IA in group 3.

Two independent school hosts of the matching IB briefs confirm four shared unit headings and AO1–AO4. The outline stops at units because the SL and HL subtopic lists differ; it does not imply identical depth at both levels.

Objective descriptions are Albus’s own second-person paraphrases. HL extensions and policy recommendations retain their HL restriction, and the commentary requirement retains its IA scope. The briefs publish assessment-component percentages, not whole-subject per-AO ranges, so objective weights remain null.
